full_judgment:
"Section 3(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code provides that in every enactment passed before the Cr.P.C. came into force in 1898 the expression"Magistrate of the district" shall be deemed to mean"District Magistrate.” Since the Arms Act came into force in 1878 before the Code of Criminal Procedure came into force, the expression "Magistrate of a district" preceded by the word "any" as used in section18 of the Arms Act shall be deemed to mean any District Magistrate. The expression "by any authority to which he may be subordinate" plainly and clearly means the superior officers to whom the officer granting the licence is subordinate. So if a District Magistrate has granted the licence, such a licence can only be cancelled or suspended by the District Magistrate by whom the same was granted or by authority to whom the said District Magistrate is subordinate when, for reasons to be recorded in writing, such District Magistrate or his superior authority deems it necessary for the security of the public peace to cancel or suspend such licence. In the case of Hakim Nawab Ali Vs. King-Emperor, A.I.R. 1946 Allahabad 484-47 Cr.L.J. 1946 page 638 Bennet, J. delivering the judgment of the Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court observed: 

 "We accordingly accept the reference and quash the conviction of Hakim S. Nawab Ali under section 19(f) of the Arms Act and the sentence of fine imposed there-under:"
